_meta.indication: Indicated in combination with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor for the treatment of hyperuricemia associated with gout in patients who have not achieved target serum uric acid levels with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor alone

pivotal_trials.design: 12-month multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized 1:1:1 to lesinurad 200 mg, lesinurad 400 mg, or placebo on background allopurinol
pivotal_trials.population: Gout patients inadequately responsive to allopurinol: on a stable dose of allopurinol of at least 300 mg with serum uric acid > 6.5 mg/dL and at least 2 gout flares in the prior 12 months
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving serum uric acid < 6.0 mg/dL at Month 6
pivotal_trials.n: N=607 randomized/enrolled (PBO 203 / LESU200 202 / LESU400 202); ITT population N=201 per arm
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 6, sUA < 6.0 mg/dL achieved by 54.23% on lesinurad 200 mg vs 27.86% on placebo (difference 0.26; 95% CI 0.17, 0.36)

nct_ctgov.title: Combining Lesinurad With Allopurinol in Inadequate Responders

pivotal_trials.design: 12-month global multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized 1:1:1 to lesinurad 200 mg, lesinurad 400 mg, or placebo on background allopurinol
pivotal_trials.population: Gout patients inadequately responsive to allopurinol with sUA levels repeatedly greater than the recommended treatment goal, on stable background allopurinol of at least 300 mg/day
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving serum uric acid < 6.0 mg/dL at Month 6
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 6, sUA < 6.0 mg/dL achieved by 55.39% on lesinurad 200 mg vs 23.30% on placebo (difference 0.32; 95% CI 0.23, 0.41)

nct_ctgov.title: Combining Lesinurad With Allopurinol in Inadequate Responders

pivotal_trials.design: 12-month global multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized 1:1:1 to lesinurad 200 mg, lesinurad 400 mg, or placebo on background febuxostat 80 mg
pivotal_trials.population: Gout patients with measurable tophi (tophaceous gout), on background febuxostat 80 mg
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving serum uric acid < 5.0 mg/dL at Month 6
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 6, sUA < 5.0 mg/dL achieved by 56.60% on lesinurad 200 mg vs 46.79% on placebo (difference 0.10; 95% CI -0.03, 0.23; p=0.13, not statistically significant)

nct_ctgov.title: Combination Treatment Study in Subjects With Tophaceous Gout With Lesinurad and Febuxostat

key_safety: Most serious risk is renal: in combination with XOI, renal failure reported in 1.2% (200 mg) vs 2.1% (placebo) and blood creatinine increased 4.3% (200 mg) vs 2.3% (placebo); monotherapy at 400 mg caused renal failure 9.3% and serum creatinine elevations >=1.5-fold in 24.3%. Most common adverse reactions with 200 mg: headache 5.3%, influenza 5.1%, gastroesophageal reflux disease 2.7%.
target_moa: Lesinurad is a URAT1 inhibitor that reduces serum uric acid by inhibiting uric acid reabsorption transporters URAT1 and OAT4 on the apical surface of renal tubular cells, increasing renal uric acid excretion

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF ACUTE RENAL FAILURE, MORE COMMON WHEN USED WITHOUT A XANTHINE OXIDASE INHIBITOR — acute renal failure has occurred with ZURAMPIC and was more common when given alone; ZURAMPIC should be used in combination with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor

rems.type: DRISK did not recommend a REMS as necessary to ensure the benefits of lesinurad 200 mg once daily in combination with a XOI outweigh the risks

advisory_committee.vote: Arthritis Advisory Committee met October 23, 2015; voted efficacy 14 yes/0 no, safety 7 yes/6 no/1 abstain, approval 10 yes/4 no

summary.text: Standard-review 505(b)(1) NDA submitted by Ardea Biosciences, received December 29, 2014, with a PDUFA goal date of December 29, 2015; approved on the date of the approval letter (signed December 22, 2015) following an Arthritis Advisory Committee meeting on October 23, 2015, with a required postmarketing renal/cardiovascular safety trial. No accelerated approval or expedited designations were applied.

citations.quote: Ardea Biosciences submitted this 505(b)(1) NDA to support approval of the use of lesinurad tablet at a dose of 200 mg once daily in combination with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor for the treatment of hyperuricemia associated with gout.

Date of Submission: December 29, 2014

PDUPA Goal Date: December 29, 2015
A meeting of the Arthritis Advisory Committee (AAC) was held on October 23, 2015, to discuss this application.
Therefore, based on appropriate scientific data, FDA has determined that you are required to conduct the following:

requirement.text: Study 3014-1: A randomized, controlled clinical trial to evaluate the safety of lesinurad 200 mg on background XOI with respect to renal function and renal adverse events, enriched with moderate renal impairment patients, minimum 2-year treatment duration, including adjudicated assessment of cardiovascular safety

citations.quote: A randomized, controlled, clinical trial to evaluate the safety of lesinurad 200mg on a background of concomitant xanthine oxidase inhibitor, with respect to renal function and renal adverse events, in gout patients who have not achieved target serum uric acid with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor alone. Enrollment should be enriched with patients with moderate renal impairment (creatinine clearance 30 to 60 mL/min). The minimum treatment duration should be 2 years. The trial must also include an assessment of cardiovascular (CV) safety based on an independent adjudication of prospectively defined and collected CV events.
